title: Results that change with partitioning and timing
verdict: double `SUM`/`AVG`, `BIGINT` sum overflow, `first`/`last`, `collect_list`, sort and window ties
description: Spark runs each partition's partial aggregate in a task and merges them in the order the tasks finish, so these depend on the partitioning and can change from run to run: the order of a double `sum` and `avg` (spark-sum-double), whether a `BIGINT` partial sum overflows (spark-sum-int), the row `first`, `last`, `any_value` take and the order `collect_list` and `string_agg` keep (spark-first-last), and the order of ties in sorts and windows (spark-sort-stability, spark-window-values). The probes caught a sort's ties in a different order on two runs.
reference: The reference compares results as bags, so row order outside a sort is free; `sum_order` is open and allowed within the plan's bound; `tie_pick` and `tie_order` allow any choice. Every Spark behaviour here is allowed but for the `BIGINT` sum, which `sverify.sql.spark` computes in decimals.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 3902 of 3902 results as the fact says.
It exercises the sums and averages with spark.sql.leafNodeDefaultParallelism at 1, 2 and 3, each scan slice summed in input order and the partials merged in either order.

aggregates[0]: 300 rows, `sum(x)`, `avg(x)`, `max(x)`, `min(x)`, 2880 of 2880 results as the fact says; int_sums[0]: 300 rows, `sum(x)`, `try_sum(x)`, 858 of 858 results as the fact says (raised: ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW 18); int_sums[2]: 300 rows, `avg(x)`, 164 of 164 results as the fact says.
Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.12.1, Linux amd64, local[2], session time zone UTC.
